verdict.rationale: Antigravity documents its own CLI sandbox: files that are not explicitly mounted are invisible, and sensitive files like .env are blocked. Git worktree support also lets agents work in isolated folders, which keeps test runs away from the main working tree. The evidence only covers filesystem isolation for the CLI and gives no detail on separating production data or databases. Community reports of .env access concern the IDE's default settings, not the documented CLI sandbox. missing for 10: documented separation of production versus test data and services, sandbox coverage beyond the CLI (IDE/desktop), in-depth sandbox docs, and independent hands-on corroboration that the sandbox holds.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Sensitive files like ~/.ssh and .env are blocked, anything not explicitly mounted is invisible inside the sandbox
Projects natively support Git worktrees, allowing agents to operate in isolated background folders.
